exact_excerpts.text: Every character gets a feat at the 1st level, the 3rd level, and every 3 Heroic levels after (for a total of 7 at Heroic level 20.)
Every character gets a feat at the 21st level - the first Epic level - and every 3 Epic levels after (for a total of 6 at Epic level 36.) Epic and standard feats can be selected for these.
Every character gets an Epic Destiny feat at level 22, 25, 28, 31 and 34.
Every character gets a Legendary feat at level 30.

Some classes automatically gain free class feats based on class level; check each class' page for more details on those. Sometimes they allow the player to make a choice of which to take, as with rogue special abilities, ranger favored enemies, and monk philosophy paths. Those feats will not be listed on this page and are described within the appropriate class pages, even though they are treated as feats for some gameplay purposes such as swapping them by spending dragonshards.

exact_excerpts.context: Introduction, additional feats: Humans and Purple Dragon Knights
exact_excerpts.text: Humans and Purple Dragon Knights get one additional generic feat at 1st level.
A standard Monk gets a bonus feat at Monk levels 1, 2, and 6 taken from a list of martial arts feats.
A standard Rogue gets a bonus feat at Rogue levels 10, 13, 16, and 19 from the list of Rogue special abilities.

Some feats have prerequisites that your character must meet to qualify for. These requisites often take the form of minimum Ability or Skill scores, or other feats. Feats with Ability prerequisites only take into account the following bonuses:

directly_supported: The introduction distinguishes generic feat slots, Epic Destiny feat slots, Legendary feat slots, and class-granted feats.

exact_excerpts.text: Usage: Passive
Prerequisite: Level 27

If you pass within 5 feet of a trap, you make a search check to notice it as if actively searching. You must be able to Spot the trap to passively Search for it in this way. (You still need the Trapfinding feat to successfully Search for difficult traps.)
Shiradi Champion: Pierce Deception automatically grants this feat. If you possess both this feat and the enhancement, then you gain an additional 5% Doubleshot.
Provides Auto-Search without penalty. Still requires a successful Spot check followed by Search check.
Watchful Eye cannot detect secret doors, only traps.

The article does not describe repeatedly selecting Watchful Eye or duplicate selections of the feat itself.
do_not_infer: The coexistence synergy is not by itself proof of a particular feat-selection UI behavior or selection order.

exact_excerpts.text: Tomes of Universal Enhancement grant extra Action Points that can be used in universal enhancements trees, such as Harper Agent enhancements.

Entwined with the words of this thick book is a powerful magical effect that grants a permanent +1 inherent bonus to Universal Enhancement Points. This effect will not stack with other Tomes of Universal Enhancement (of the same source) but will with Tomes of Universal Enhancement from other sources.

Tome of Universal Enhancement +1 (Sharn) was introduced with Masterminds of Sharn expansion. The ultimate bundle grants a tome to each character. In September 2019, the tome became available in the DDO Store for 3495 DP.

Tome of Universal Enhancement +1 (Morgrave) was introduced with Vecna Unleashed expansion. The ultimate bundle grants a tome to each character. In March 2024, the tome became available in the DDO Store for 3495 DP.

Tome of Universal Enhancement +1 (Lamordia) was introduced with The Chill of Ravenloft expansion. The ultimate bundle grants a tome to each character. In January 2026, the tome became available in the DDO Store for 2995 DP.

Tome of Universal Enhancement +1 (Demogorgon) was introduced with the Terror of Demogorgon expansion. The ultimate bundle grants a tome to each character. In January 2027, the tome became available in the DDO Store for 3495 DP.
Unlike Tome of Enhancement (Racial), this tome is *NOT* displayed in the character sheet > feats > special feats. To check if the tome was applied, check the enhancement page.
exact_excerpts.formatting_note: Asterisks around NOT reflect emphasis as supplied by the capture.

exact_excerpts.text: This tome is Bound to Character on Acquire, so you must be sure you don’t have it already on the toon you buy it with (and it’s the toon you want to use it on).

acquisition_rows.representation: Structured transcription of retained source values, also preserved in exact source excerpts above.

source_inconsistencies.subject: Demogorgon store acquisition date
source_inconsistencies.observed_claim: January 2027 store availability is described in past tense.
source_inconsistencies.issue: The claimed date is later than the observation date. The source claim is preserved; availability as of observation is not established by this sentence.

directly_supported: Each tome grants a permanent +1 inherent bonus to Universal Enhancement Points.
Tomes from the same source do not stack; different sources stack.
The introduction explicitly names universal enhancement trees and Harper Agent enhancements as a permitted destination for the extra AP.
The page's supplied Notes say to check the enhancement page to determine whether the tome has been applied.
unresolved: This source does not state level/access timing for spending its granted points.
This source does not establish whether Harper Agent has been unlocked on a particular character or account.
This source does not establish the prerequisites of any specific Harper enhancement.

cross_source_inference.status: Inference, not an explicit statement on this tome page
cross_source_inference.premise_from_this_page: Tome points can be used in universal enhancement trees, explicitly including Harper Agent.
cross_source_inference.other_source_exact_text: These bonus AP are not level-gated - a character can spend them all at level 1.
cross_source_inference.conclusion: Taken together, the two pages support spending these bonus points at level 1 in eligible Harper nodes when Harper is already unlocked and the node's requirements are met.
cross_source_inference.excluded_claim: The tome itself is not shown here to unlock Harper Agent, waive node prerequisites, or establish the character's existing access.

evidence.title: Favored Enemy

permanent_link.limitation: Value was truncated in the normal-page observation; historical URL not opened.

exact_excerpts.text: At first level a Ranger selects a type of creature from the favored enemy list. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter (10th, 15th, and 20th) the Ranger selects an additional creature type from the favored enemy list. When fighting a Favored Enemy, you gain +2 Damage for each Favored Enemy feat you have. If you have more than one Favored Enemy feat that applies to a particular Enemy, the damage applies for each type that matches a favored Enemy feat you have.
If a creature is affected by two Favored Enemy selections (such as a Chaotic Evil Outsider attacked by a character with both FE: Chaotic Outsider and FE: Evil Outsider) then both effects stack
exact_excerpts.source_note: The supporting source link is marked UPDATE ME.

exact_excerpts.text: If a non-Ranger Gnome character has Undead as a Favored Enemy from the Vistani enhancement tree, and Reptilian from the Gnome Racial enhancement tree, they do +4 damage to both those Favored Enemies.
If that same Gnome character was a Level 20 Ranger, they would also have their 5 base Favored enemies from 20 Ranger Levels, for +14 to all 7 Favored Enemies.

That same Level 20(+) Gnome Ranger might also have 1 additional favored enemy from Deepwood Stalker enhancements, 1 from the Harper enhancement tree, 1 from the Falconry enhancement tree, 1 from Horizon Walker enhancement tree plus 1 from the Shiradi Champion Epic Destiny tree, as well as the 7 from the previous example (Vistani & Gnome & Ranger 20), for a total of 12 Favored Enemies; that character then does +24 extra damage to all favored enemies.
Horizon Walker capstone gives "Favored Enemy: Marked Target".
exact_excerpts.source_note: The supporting forum link is marked UPDATE ME.

The page describes damage stacking when two different matching enemy types overlap.
Marked Target is explicitly named as a Horizon Walker capstone Favored Enemy.

exact_excerpts.text: Bow attack: Fire three arrows in quick succession. You have +2 Critical Threat Range and Critical Multiplier with these shots. Passive: You gain Doubleshot equal to 1.5x your Base Attack Bonus with Longbows and Shortbows.
